title: Delight in the details
principle: Spend care on micro-interactions, focus states, and edge copy that most users only notice when missing—polish is a signal of respect.
procedure: List five moments a careful user will touch (focus, empty, error, success, hover).
Design each moment intentionally; ban default browser leftovers where brand matters.
Add one surprise of restraint (not fireworks)—timing, easing, or copy.
Verify keyboard and reduced-motion paths feel equally considered.
Cut any delight that slows a frequent action (novelty vs frequency).
examplePrompts:
Polish the five touch moments on this UI: focus, empty, error, success, hover.

For each: intended feel in 5 words; motion ≤200ms or none; copy rewrite.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Do not add confetti to primary flows.
promptWhy: Turns vague ‘make it nice’ into a checklist of moments.
tips: Comeau’s public writing obsesses over CSS details that feel good in the hand.
Pair with Rauno’s novelty restraint for high-frequency actions.

workedExamples.title: Default focus ring shame
workedExamples.after: Visible, on-brand focus that still passes contrast.

workedExamples.title: Empty state shrug
workedExamples.after: One human sentence + one clear next action.
workedExamples.body: Empty states are product moments, not absences.

antiPatterns: Delight on the most frequent action that needs speed.
checklist: No noisy delight on high-frequency actions.

useWhen: The current deliver task needs this specific principle: Spend care on micro-interactions, focus states, and edge copy that most users only notice when missing—polish is a signal of respect.
inputs: A concrete user problem and the current artifact
Constraints, existing behavior and source attribution to preserve
agentContract.output: A bounded application of “Delight in the details” with before/after evidence and remaining limitations.
agentContract.recipe:
1. List five moments a careful user will touch (focus, empty, error, success, hover).
2. Design each moment intentionally; ban default browser leftovers where brand matters.
3. Add one surprise of restraint (not fireworks)—timing, easing, or copy.
4. Verify keyboard and reduced-motion paths feel equally considered.
5. Cut any delight that slows a frequent action (novelty vs frequency).
acceptance: Show the before/after artifact and explain how “Delight in the details” improves the named user task.

stateRequirements.responsive: Check 390px and desktop plus 200% zoom; preserve reading order, wrap long text and keep actions reachable.
stateRequirements.accessibility: Use semantic headings and native controls, visible labels and focus; normal text contrast at least 4.5:1.
stateRequirements.keyboard: Complete the primary action using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter and Space; no pointer-only information or focus trap.
stateRequirements.reducedMotion: Remove nonessential movement; preserve all state and information without waiting for animation.
stateRequirements.loading: Show pending feedback only during real work; retain context and allow navigation away.
stateRequirements.empty: Distinguish no content from no matching results; explain how to proceed or reset filters.
stateRequirements.error: Explain the failed action, retain user input and offer recovery; never claim success on failure.
stateRequirements.interruption: A newer action wins; cancel or ignore stale results and keep controls responsive.
stateRequirements.stateChange: Announce important results politely without moving focus unexpectedly.

compatibility.rule: Start with one technique. Add at most one companion for a distinct unsolved problem; candidates are suggestions, not verified compatibility.
conflicts: Two techniques changing the same visual role require an explicit winner.
Do not combine multiple entrance or attention effects on one target.
Aesthetic subtraction must not remove semantics, feedback or attribution.
compatibility.stop: Stop when the named task is clearer and acceptance evidence is recorded; do not add polish without a problem.
